categories.main_business_segments: U-Haul Holding Company operates three primary business segments: (1) Moving and Storage, which includes truck, trailer, and equipment rentals, self-storage, portable moving/storage units, and related retail products; (2) Property and Casualty Insurance, which provides insurance products and claims handling for U-Haul customers and affiliates; and (3) Life Insurance, which offers life, Medicare supplement, and annuity products primarily to the senior market.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: U-Haul designs and manufactures its own rental trucks and trailers, featuring proprietary technologies such as the Lowest Deck, Gentle Ride Suspension, and Mom’s Attic for ease of use and safety. The company operates 11 manufacturing and assembly facilities and 151 repair centers, and leverages a proprietary reservations management system and digital platforms (uhaul.com, U-Haul app) for customer engagement and fleet management.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are 'do-it-yourself' household movers, including individuals, families, students, and small businesses needing moving, storage, or towing solutions. U-Haul also serves commercial customers, independent dealers, and the senior market through its insurance products.
categories.geographic_coverage: U-Haul operates throughout the United States and Canada, with over 2,200 company-operated retail locations, nearly 21,300 independent dealers, and 1,904 self-storage facilities. Its insurance operations and digital platforms also serve customers across North America.
categories.supply_chain_position: U-Haul operates primarily at the downstream end of the supply chain, directly serving end customers with rental equipment, storage, and retail products, while also managing a large network of independent dealers and affiliates.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the independent dealer and storage affiliate networks, investing in digital and mobile technologies (such as Truck Share 24/7 and the U-Haul app), enhancing customer convenience, and sustainability initiatives like equipment sharing and manufacturing reusable/recyclable products. The company is also preparing for future trends in electric and alternative-fuel vehicles and expanding its insurance offerings.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through rental fees for trucks, trailers, and self-storage units, sales of moving and storage products, towing accessories, and propane, as well as insurance premiums and property management fees. Digital services and online marketplaces (Moving Help, U-Box, Storage Affiliates) also contribute to revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In truck rentals, major competitors include Avis Budget Group and Penske Truck Leasing; in self-storage, key competitors are Public Storage, CubeSmart, Extra Space Storage, and Life Storage. U-Haul is the largest 'do-it-yourself' moving and storage operator in North America, with a broad geographic footprint and extensive dealer network.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2023, consolidated revenue was $5.86 billion, with the Moving and Storage segment accounting for nearly 95% of revenue. The company operates a large asset base ($18.1 billion in total assets) and maintains significant liquidity. While self-storage and U-Box revenues grew, overall earnings declined year-over-year due to higher operating and repair costs and slower fleet rotation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: U-Haul emphasizes convenience, broad geographic coverage, and a comprehensive 'one-stop' solution for moving and storage needs. Proprietary equipment features, extensive digital platforms, and a large network of locations and affiliates differentiate U-Haul, along with a focus on sustainability and customer-centric innovations like contactless rentals and integrated moving services.
